findings.title: Authorization logic uses AND instead of OR for team admin/owner check
findings.body: The condition `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` requires the user to be BOTH a team admin AND a team owner. The intent is clearly that either role should be sufficient (i.e., `||`). As written, a team admin who is not an owner (or vice versa) will be denied access to add guests unless they also happen to be the organizer or an attendee. This effectively breaks the feature for most team members.

findings.title: Email sending uses unfiltered `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input `guests` array, but `uniqueGuests` is the filtered list that was actually added to the booking (excluding already-existing attendees and blacklisted emails). Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the `newGuests` parameter is used to decide whether to send a full 'scheduled' email (to new guests) or a 'guests added' notification (to existing attendees). If some input emails were filtered out (e.g., duplicates of existing attendees), those existing attendees will incorrectly receive a full scheduled email instead of the notification.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails does not respect eventType email disable settings
findings.body: Unlike peer functions such as `sendLocationChangeEmails` and `sendCancelledEmails`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept or check `eventTypeMetadata` for `disableStandardEmails` settings. Users who have disabled host or attendee emails at the event type level will still receive add-guests emails, violating their configured preferences.

findings.title: Initial state of [""] causes spurious validation error on empty submit
findings.body: `multiEmailValue` is initialized to `[""]` (array containing one empty string). When the user clicks 'Add' without entering any email, `multiEmailValue.length` is 1, so the early-return guard on line 49 does not trigger. The Zod schema then fails validation on the empty string, showing the user an 'Emails must be unique and valid' error even though they haven't entered anything. The initial state should be `[]` or the guard should also check for empty/whitespace-only strings.

findings.title: addGuests uses authedProcedure instead of bookingsProcedure
findings.body: The `editLocation` endpoint uses `bookingsProcedure` which likely includes additional booking-specific authorization or middleware. The new `addGuests` endpoint uses the more permissive `authedProcedure`. While the handler performs its own authorization check, this inconsistency means any cross-cutting concerns handled by `bookingsProcedure` (e.g., booking existence checks, rate limiting, audit logging) are bypassed for this endpoint.

findings.title: Organizer email subject uses attendees[0].name which may be a newly added guest with empty name
findings.body: The subject line uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` for the `{{name}}` interpolation. Since newly added guests have `name: ""` (set in the handler), if a new guest happens to be first in the attendees array, the subject will read 'Guests Added: <eventType> with  at <date>' with a blank name. The original booking's primary attendee or organizer name would be more appropriate.
